description: Present advantage transfers ecological fiscal and institutional burden to future people.
Infrastructure public health education and environmental systems fail after chronic underinvestment.
Opaque AI surveillance and platform systems become difficult for future people to contest or remove.
Continuous crisis erodes planning capacity and future-oriented governance.
Climate repair is promised but finance implementation and legal duties remain insufficient.
Actors benefiting from inherited inequality resist repair and future-generation duties.
Youth participation exists but remains advisory symbolic or disconnected from formal authority.
Long-term stewardship institutions weaken over time without political and budgetary support.
